newsitem.title: GERMANY: Too early to call Krupp bid hostile - Deutsche Bank.
newsitem.headline: Too early to call Krupp bid hostile - Deutsche Bank.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG management board member Rolf Breuer said on Tuesday it was too early to describe Krupp AG's 435 marks per share bid for Thyssen as hostile since Thyssen had not yet made any recommendation to its shareholders on the bid.

Breuer noted to reporters at a news conference on asset management that Thyssen's management and supervisory board had yet to comment on the bid presented, and had yet to make a recommendation to shareholders.
"If Thyssen told its shareholders 'we recommend not accepting the bid' and Krupp persists with its offer, only then do we have a hostile bid," Breuer said.
Breuer described media reports of a hostile bid as "a bit premature".
Breuer declined to specify the extent of the financing Krupp would need for the takeover, saying this depended on how many shareholders would take up the offer.
He also declined to comment on what action Deutsche Bank would take if Thyssen rejected the offer.

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell is among three investment banks who are advising Krupp on its bid for Thyssen. Deutsche, Dresdner Bank AG and Goldman Sachs and other banks are securing financing for the deal.

Breuer also said German industry was entering a phase of stronger concentration ahead of European monetary union and he was very interested in the Thyssen takeover proceeding in an orderly fashion along the lines of takeovers in the U.K. and U.S., where such events were more common.

"I very much want this first large case in Germany to proceed in an orderly fashion and hope that it demonstrates that the German financial centre is also in a position to carry out a takeover in a manner that is common in other countries.
Breuer noted that the Krupp bid was "extraordinary" by German standards in terms of its volume, participants and economic background.
"In Britain and the U.S., such transactions are more common, or at least not extraordinary," he said.
